title: Network coordinator worker Batch 3 lifecycle provider semantics
summary: Implemented Batch 3 network coordinator/worker lifecycle and provider semantics fixes: cooperative ordinary stop, active-work dry-run evidence, two-phase worker polling startup, PowerShell worker-result artifact consumption for network done reports, local_worker_result QueueTerminal/Retryable fields, and stale result archive durability.
reason: The review found that ordinary Network stops could abort active work, dry-runs hid active in-memory claims, worker polling could claim before provider attachment, network worker completion ignored PowerShell result artifacts, local_worker_result lacked retry/terminal evidence, and stale result diagnostics could be deleted on slot reuse.
behavior_before: Ordinary worker/coordinator stop killed or released active work; lifecycle dry-runs did not report active in-memory jobs; worker polling started during dispatcher construction; network done reports used process exit code instead of local_worker_result evidence; PowerShell result payloads omitted QueueTerminal/Retryable; stale per-slot worker_result.json could be overwritten on reuse.
behavior_after: Ordinary stop stops polling/new claims and preserves active process/claim state until done reporting; dry-runs expose active jobs and review/block posture; provider startup attaches app dispatcher and runtime before polling; network done reports validate and map local_worker_result fields; PowerShell result payloads include QueueTerminal/Retryable; stale worker results are archived before repair/reuse deletion.
tests_added: PowerShell local worker slot/result schema and stale-result archive regressions
Python provider/lifecycle/done regressions for cooperative stop, dry-run active evidence, two-phase worker startup, result-artifact mapping, and retryability
